rationale: B wins because it stays closer to the supplied facts. Its 'Whoop's new blood-pressure number isn't a medical reading — and needs a cuff to even start' angle is sharp without inventing a market, medical, or funding story; A's 'Whoop Finally Has FDA-Cleared ECG. Apple Watch Has Had It for Years.' smuggles in a named competitor and timeline the update did not give. A has one excellent regulatory angle, but B is the cleaner founder handoff: fewer details waiting to become corrections.
gaps_in_A: 'Whoop Finally Has FDA-Cleared ECG. Apple Watch Has Had It for Years.' names Apple and asserts timing that the update did not supply. The update only says competitors already ship FDA-cleared ECG.

'Apple Watch includes ECG with hardware, no subscription gate — confirm this' admits the access angle rests on an unconfirmed competitor-pricing premise. Do not make the comparison do load-bearing work until it is verified.

'AFib Detection on Your Wrist Is Now a Premium Feature — and That's a Health Equity Story' is promising but a little inflated. Without the exact tier price, competitor pricing, and access impact, 'health equity' risks becoming moral garnish.
'The wearable industry has spent years positioning cuffless blood pressure monitoring as the next frontier' may be true, but it is not in the update. Source it or cut it.
gaps_in_B: 'what Whoop's screenless-band ECG does differently from a wrist-screen device' introduces a product-detail premise the update did not provide. Verify the screenless/form-factor point before using it.

B misses the clean standalone regulatory angle in A: the FDA-cleared ECG sitting beside a non-medical BP 'wellness estimate.' It folds that into consumer accountability, which works, but leaves a medtech/FDA-boundary story underdeveloped.

'health features are increasingly paywalled' needs more than this one launch. B correctly says the trend needs proof, but the angle still needs competitor examples before it can carry a week-long trend frame.
'journalist-fit-check' is a slightly premature next step for the whole set. Names can wait until the price, competitor list, FDA language, and disclaimer wording are nailed down.
